In the code, each call to `nextToken()` is preceded by a check (either `hasMoreElements()` or `hasMoreTokens()`) that ensures there is at least one token left. Specifically:
- First call to `tokenizer.nextToken()` (line with `idAndDirection`) is after `if (!tokenizer.hasMoreElements()) return null;`.
- Second call on `idAndDirTokenizer.nextToken()` (for `extIDStr`) is after `if (!idAndDirTokenizer.hasMoreElements()) return null;`.
- Third call on `idAndDirTokenizer.nextToken()` (for `direction`) is after `if (!idAndDirTokenizer.hasMoreTokens()) return null;`.
- Fourth call on `tokenizer.nextToken()` (for `uriStr`) is after `if (!tokenizer.hasMoreElements()) return null;`.
- Fifth call on `tokenizer.nextToken()` (for `extensionAttributes`) is inside `if (tokenizer.hasMoreElements())`, so it only executes when a token exists.
Therefore, all calls to `nextToken()` are guarded, and the `NoSuchElementException` is avoided in every case.
